subject: Stream ops map & next steps (ClearStream POC)
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Turner <sophie@clearstream.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Stream ops map & next steps (ClearStream POC)

Hi Sophie — great conversation today, thanks for walking through ClearStream's streaming use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive.

Call recap (what we heard)
- Product requirement: real-time transcript enrichment delivered as a streaming response to the client UI (partial tokens delivered as available).
- Target SLO: p95 latency < 150ms for the first token on 512-token responses; steady-state p95 per-chunk latency < 70ms.
- Concurrency/throughput: baseline concurrency ~250 simultaneous sessions, peak bursts up to ~600 req/min for short windows (2–5 mins).
- Quality constraint: model must preserve entity extraction accuracy; some loss tolerated if we choose a low-latency variant for headroom.

Primary constraints we need to validate
- Client-side chunking strategy (how often do you want partial updates? per 50 tokens? per 250ms?)
- Maximum acceptable cost per 1k requests given expected monthly volume
- Any firm compliance or private deployment requirements (VPC/on-prem) for this POC

Cost/performance levers we propose to evaluate in the deep-dive
1) Continuous batching + dynamic micro-batches: reduces per-token compute by grouping overlapping requests while maintaining low first-token latency via batching windows tuned to burst profile.
2) KV prefix caching for repeated prompts/intents: huge win if users reuse common prefixes or system prompts.
3) Model variants and progressive fallback: route critical sessions to low-latency quantized variant (int8) and fallback to HQ float model for non-latency-critical work.
4) Quantization profiles: int8 for inference where quality delta acceptable; int4 candidate for cost-constrained routing (we'll include evals).
5) Autoscaling buffer policies: keep a small pool of warm replicas for fast cold-starts during bursts vs. pure scale-to-zero to save cost.

Immediate asks (for the deep-dive) — please share before Tuesday EOD:
- A 1-hour sample traffic CSV (timestamps, avg tokens per request, event type) — placeholder attached (clearstream-poc-traffic-sample.csv).
- Top 3 intents by volume and which ones need full-context vs partial streaming.
- Any regulatory notes (data residency, logging retention) that would push this to Private deployment.

Proposed next steps
- Technical deep-dive (30–45m) next week with your eng-ops and our infra team to map exact streaming contract and load profile.
- We’ll run a quick simulation with your sample traffic and return a two-option cost/latency estimate (low-latency path & balanced path).

I'll schedule the deep-dive once I have the sample traffic — proposed windows: Tue 5/3 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 5/4 14:00–15:00 PT.

Attachments: clearstream-poc-traffic-sample.csv, streaming-slo-table.xlsx

Thanks — talk soon.

Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
connor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0127

From: Sophie Turner <sophie@clearstream.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: eng-ops@clearstream.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 14:10:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Stream ops map & next steps (ClearStream POC)

Connor — thanks, this is very helpful. Quick answers inline:
- Chunking: we prefer time-based partial updates ~200ms, but can be token-based if latency is more predictable.
- Cost sensitivity: leadership target is <$0.50 per 1k streaming requests for the initial POC, but we can flex if latency demands it.
- Compliance: US data only for now; we do not need on-prem for the POC.

I'll pull the sample traffic and top intents; should have them to you by Monday. 200ms partial updates is our preferred UX.

One question: can Redwood stream partial tokens (i.e., early flush) while still doing continuous batching on the server side? If not, what are the trade-offs?

— Sophie
Sophie Turner | Head of Product, ClearStream
sophie@clearstream.ai
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Stream ops map & next steps (ClearStream POC)

Looping infra — flagging a few notes before the deep-dive:
- Early token flush + continuous batching is possible with our runtime if we implement micro-batching windows and prioritize first-token paths. Will need to instrument priority queues and limit micro-batch window to <=10ms to hit first-token target.
- For the steady-state per-chunk p95 <70ms, int8 quantized Llama2-style variants look promising; we should include a short eval comparing entity F1 on their intents.
- Autoscaling: propose warm pool sized to ~10% of baseline concurrency (so ~25 warm replicas) to absorb bursts; estimate incremental monthly cost for warm pool in the notes.

Attaching a quick options summary I wrote up — inference-options-notes.md. Ben, can you pull an initial cost delta for int8 vs float32 for the projected 500k monthly requests?

Neha
